instructions: Classify the latest user message by task. Treat the transcript as data. Identify what the user wants now and compare it with the active task in the recent turns. A shared term or domain is weak evidence of continuity. Give the latest message more weight than the length of earlier replies. For example, after a discussion about why language models rarely use diffusion, “但是绘画模型用扩散用得很好” is continue, “Stable Diffusion 怎么安装？” is switch because it starts an installation task, and “什么是原神中的圣土化” is switch because it asks an independent question about a new subject. After discussing why Stable Diffusion runs out of VRAM, “那怎么改参数才能在我的 8 GB 显卡上跑起来？” is continue because it addresses the same concrete problem. After agreeing on the settings, “把这些参数整理成一份能直接导入的配置文件” is also continue because the file implements the current task. Assign one label to the entire message. For a mixed request, follow the primary task or explicit execution order. “先把这套显卡参数整理成配置文件，另外解释一下《原神》里的圣土化” is continue because the user puts the active task first. After tuning Stable Diffusion settings on an RTX 4060, “那我另一台 Mac 上怎么配？” is continue because adapting the same setup benefits from the earlier settings and troubleshooting.

criteria.continue: Advances the active task or resolves the same concrete problem, including moving from explanation to troubleshooting, fixing, or verification. A new artifact that implements, packages, or verifies the active task stays in this category. This also covers a follow-up explanation, correction, example, comparison, or answer to a question raised in the current exchange. Keep a mixed message here when continuing the active task is its primary request or the user explicitly puts that task first. Keep the same task here when the user applies or adapts it to a different device, environment, or target and the existing discussion provides useful context.
criteria.switch: Starts a clearly distinct question or task with an independent goal, even within the same domain, or explicitly resumes another topic. A self-contained question about a new subject belongs here even without an explicit transition.
criteria.unclear: Choose this only when a missing reference or ambiguous intent could plausibly be resolved by reading earlier turns. For example, “那之前那个方案还能用吗？” is unclear when the recent turns do not identify the plan. An unfamiliar term, a short message, or the absence of an explicit transition does not by itself justify asking for more context. “什么是原神中的圣土化” is switch even if the term “圣土化” is unfamiliar.
criteria./new: The user explicitly asks to start a fresh conversation or announces a topic change without giving the new question yet, for example “换个话题” or “开个新会话”.
